rules: Show all three levels together; include full titles when helpful for a handoff or status report.
Represent the actual main-stage, remediation-group and lettered-batch statuses independently. Completing a batch does not automatically complete FR.2 or Stage3.
The current hierarchy is Stage3 > FR.2 > current lettered batch. Other FR groups may span other roadmap stages; do not assume FR number equals stage number.
Stage3/10 and FR.2/8 identify position/endpoint, not completed counts or percentages. The roadmap also contains Stage0.

U is accepted COMPLETE (FRE195); BatchV/Z remains ON_HOLD during owner phone transfer and stays open until its defined acceptance evidence passes. A successful local verifier is LOCAL_CHECKS_COMPLETE with hosted acceptance pending; it is not whole-batch COMPLETE.
STARTED, COMPLETE and STOPPED_FOR_REVIEW must identify the action/phase they describe. If updating a document or output convention, say that action completed while retaining the actual batch status.
On failure keep the same batch letter and STOPPED_FOR_REVIEW; do not advance or silently add letters. Preserve prior results and inspect uncertain writes before retry.

After a batch completes, report the completed batch with COMPLETE. When real work starts in the next batch, update the current letter/status and remaining-work ledger; do not show a future planned batch as already completed.

New human-readable terminal output should include the hierarchy on STARTED/COMPLETE/STOPPED_FOR_REVIEW lines. New safe JSON may add a validated progress_context with these public labels/statuses and an explicit action/phase status.

Keep exact result/test counts, local versus hosted scope, checked timestamps, exit codes and uncertainty fields alongside this display. Progress labels replace none of the safety or acceptance evidence.
Keep pinned historical scripts/receipts unchanged. Do not retrofit old output, invalidate old manifests, repeat installations/emails/uploads or rerun successful acceptance just to add labels.
Continue to explain every owner-command effect/prompt, use published pins, keep private inputs hidden, and end runnable owner instructions with Send me the safe JSON and exit code.

An explicit owner instruction may hold an incomplete package while independent work starts in another planned letter. Show the held package and dependent blocked cases; never label it complete or bypass its controls. Owner deferred V MFA on26October; W read-only Auth review can proceed, Admin-dependent W/Z acceptance stays blocked.
